narrative: Today's ecology literature leans heavily on fire and climate change, with modelling work projecting a nearly 39% rise in European burned area by 2100 as fire weather increasingly outpaces management capacity, while a multispecies seed-addition experiment showed range shifts lagging climate change at species' leading elevational edges but not their trailing ones. In food-web ecology, a new isotope-based superposition method promises faster reconstruction of trophic positions, and a 1,309-site metagenomic survey linked cyanobacterial blooms to synchronised trophic cascades across multiple levels. Invasion biology saw crayfish shown to reorganise, rather than simply shift, their environmental niche space, while a long-term Osprey dataset revealed that rare pioneering movements drive range recolonisation much as they do biological invasions. On the conservation side, two decades of Costa Rican restoration plots confirmed that active tree planting delivers far greater biomass gains than natural regeneration alone, and a new site-prioritisation framework improved survival outcomes for seeded coral restoration. Methodologically, a zero-shot learning pipeline extended frog-call classification across continents with a new Australian dataset, and a validated Bayesian model now converts nest temperature records directly into sea turtle hatchling sex ratios. Evolutionary biology contributed a global analysis of over 10,000 bird species showing plumage colour and pattern jointly track Gloger's and Bogert's climatic rules.
